conviction_note: The findings lean mildly positive (impact_sum +1.5). Short interest has more than doubled into a print where management already flagged tariff upside, and the September clothing data are firm. Against that is a new CEO's first full-quarter call, which could reset the outlook, and a 20% sell-off since mid-August. So p_up is only 55, on a 10% absolute move (option-implied 9.3% with wide spreads, own median 7.2%), giving +1.0. The two measurements agree in sign; the scaled number is smaller because this name's beats have been bought only ~+2% while its guide cuts cost about 20%.
bar: Q3 FY26 adj EPS: company guide ~$0.85, consensus $0.894 (MarketBeat, 2026-10-19, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-carters-cri-set-to-post-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/) and $0.86 (Chartmill, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/CRI/estimates). Revenue: guide ~$750m, consensus $751.5m (MarketBeat) / $756.6m (Chartmill). Adj op income guide ~$50m. Guide from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060822/000106082226000108/cri-ex991q22026.htm, 2026-07-31). FY26 guide: adj EPS down high single to low double digits from $3.47 (~$3.05-3.23), against a MarketBeat FY consensus of $3.28, which is already above the top of the guide. print_vs_bar_pct is measured on adj EPS against the ~$0.89 consensus.
positioning_check: Short interest has more than doubled since the Q2 print. FINRA via ChartExchange (https://chartexchange.com/symbol/nyse-cri/short-interest): 2026-07-31 3.11m shares (8.9% of float, 3.1 days to cover); 2026-08-31 4.57m (13.1%); 2026-09-15 5.78m (16.6%); 2026-09-30 7.57m (21.7%, 5.1 days); 2026-10-15 6.81m (19.6%, 5.2 days). That is a crowded short into the print. Skew: skew_25d_vol_points is null in the baseline, so no directional statement from options. Put/call OI 0.98; ATM IV 66%; the ATM spread is 51% of mid, so the 9.3% event-implied move is indicative only. Tape: spot $32.59, -3.95% over 5 days, +2.78% over 20 days, -26.6% from the 52-week high. Insider Form 4 tax-withholding prices were $39.06-39.96 on 8-12 August, so the stock is ~17-18% lower since mid-August. Sell side: MarketBeat reports Wells Fargo cut its target from $42 to $30 (equal weight) on 2026-10-12. BMO initiated at outperform with a $40 target on 2026-09-08. Consensus target is $39.38.

findings.finding: Short interest rose from 3.11m shares (8.9% of float, 3.1 days to cover) on 2026-07-31 to 7.57m (21.7%) on 2026-09-30 and 6.81m (19.6%, 5.2 days to cover) on 2026-10-15. That is the highest level in the 2026 series, whose January-July range was 7.6%-11.2%. It sets up a squeeze into a print guided to rising earnings (Q3 adj EPS ~$0.85 vs $0.74) with gross margin up ~200bp.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Of the last 8 prints, beats or in-line prints moved +2.06% (Q2 FY26, a $0.26 vs $0.06 EPS beat), +1.95% (Q3 FY25) and +11.67% (Q1 FY26, 2026-05-06), while guide-driven disappointments moved -20.25% (2026-02-27) and -19.69% (2025-07-25). The earlier short base (~9-11%) was much smaller, so there is no prior squeeze on this float level.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is itself the bearish positioning. What is not priced is the asymmetry: with ~5 days to cover, an in-line or better guide forces covering. If the market had priced a squeeze, short interest would have been falling into the print rather than near its high, and the stock would not sit 17% below its mid-August level with consensus EPS above the guide.
findings.independence: Wells Fargo's target cut from $42 to $30 (2026-10-12, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-carters-cri-set-to-post-earnings-on-monday-2026-10-19/) and the slide from ~$39-40 in mid-August, seen in Form 4 prices (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1060822/000106082226000117/0001060822-26-000117.txt), confirm bearish sentiment built after Q2. A different source, same direction of crowding.

findings.finding: On the 2026-07-31 call management said the full-year gross tariff cost over baseline had fallen from ~$200m (original plan) to ~$75m. It said the replacement of the Section 122 surcharge by Section 301 duties of 10-12.5% on 2026-07-24 'may have some upside to our earnings outlook' if unchanged, yet it held the FY adj EPS guide at down high single to low double digits. The Section 301 rates have stayed at 10-12.5%, with no excess-capacity tariffs imposed by late October, so the stated condition for upside has held. A firmed or raised FY guide is plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line this stock trades on. A guide withdrawal or cut cost -19.7% (2025-07-25) and -20.3% (2026-02-27), and Q1 FY26's print with reaffirmed outlook and strong comps bought +11.7%. A Q2 beat with the guide merely maintained bought +2.1%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the MarketBeat FY consensus of $3.28 already sits above the guide range (~$3.05-3.23), and Q3 consensus of $0.89 sits above the $0.85 guide, so the street has taken some of the upside. What is not priced is the guide itself moving. The stock is 17% lower since the call and short interest has doubled, which is not what a priced-in raise looks like.
findings.independence: The 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060822/000106082226000109/cri-20260704.htm) shows ~$18m of Section 122 tariff still capitalised in inventory at quarter end, flowing through Q3 cost of goods; that is already in the guide. The tariff regime after July 24 (Section 301 at 10-12.5%) is confirmed by https://textalks.com/us-tariffs-give-bangladesh-a-new-apparel-edge-over-vietnam-and-china/. Same direction, independent source on the rates.

findings.finding: Census advance retail sales (released 2026-10-15): clothing and clothing-accessory stores rose +5.0% y/y in September 2026, +4.3% in August and +4.5% for July-September vs a year earlier (flat m/m in September). Total retail rose +6.3% y/y. September is the largest month of Carter's Q3 by management's own account. July US Retail comps were flat 'in line with expectations', and the Q3 guide is total sales roughly flat with Wholesale down high single digits.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A US Retail comp of +5.1% in Q2 FY26, inside a beat, bought +2.1%. A strong comp quarter with reaffirmed outlook (Q1 FY26, +7.8% H1 comps) bought +11.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a public series and a proxy. It is nominal and includes tariff-driven price increases, and it covers all clothing stores, not children's. If the market had read it into Carter's, the stock would not have fallen -3.95% in the last five days into a quarter whose largest month printed +5% y/y for the category.
findings.independence: Proxy only; Carter's has not confirmed September trends. Target reported Q2 comps of +3.8%, with growth in all six core categories including apparel (https://corporate.target.com/news-features/article/2026/08/q2-2026-earnings, 2026-08-19), which points the same way for an earlier period.

findings.finding: Carter's two large wholesale/mass customers that reported after its last print were healthy. Target's Q2 (reported 2026-08-19) had comps +3.8%, traffic +3.6%, growth in all six core categories including apparel, and full-year sales growth ~5%. Kohl's Q2 (reported 2026-08-26) raised its FY outlook, and its call named kids as a bright spot. This supports Carter's statement that Fall and Winter wholesale bookings were up y/y, although Carter's guided Q3 Wholesale down high single digits on a Q2 pull-forward.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 Wholesale +11.7% within a beat bought +2.1%. No separate wholesale-line reaction is identifiable in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: these are August prints, well covered. The residual is that Carter's guided Q3 Wholesale down high single digits conservatively before seeing customers' August raises; a Wholesale line better than guided would not be in the stock, which has fallen since.
findings.independence: Kohl's Q2 FY26 transcript (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/KSS/Q22026) and release (https://corporate.kohls.com/news/kohls-reports-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-financial-results), a separate company.

findings.finding: The Children's Place, the closest specialty kids competitor, reported Q2 (quarter ended 2026-08-01) on 2026-09-15: net sales -18.9%, DTC comps -16.7%, blamed on traffic, conversion, a clearance-heavy mix and a delayed e-commerce replatform. Its stock fell ~23%, but it said trends began to reverse at the start of Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No identifiable Carter's reaction to competitor prints in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: It is ambiguous rather than unpriced. PLCE's causes are largely self-inflicted (replatform, clearance), which reads as share available to Carter's in back-to-school, but it can also be read as kids-category weakness. Sized near zero; filed so the judges can weigh it.
findings.independence: Census clothing stores +4.3-5.0% y/y in August-September (https://www.census.gov/retail/marts/www/marts_current.pdf) says the category was not weak overall, which supports the share-shift reading.

findings.finding: Sharon Price John became CEO on 2026-06-15 and was five weeks in on the Q2 call. There she said she had not yet met with the board on plans and was 'reticent' to lay out next steps, while stating the company will become 'consumer-centric and data-driven' with brand building. Q3 (2026-10-30) is her first full quarter and the natural moment for a strategic plan, which could include reinvestment in marketing or brand, a 2027 framework below the street, or a reset in guide or dividend.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance resets are the largest moves in the baseline: -20.25% (2026-02-27, margin compression and cautious outlook) and -19.69% (2025-07-25, guide withdrawn and dividend cut). The prior CEO transition announcement on 2026-05-01 moved -1.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the doubling of short interest and the slide since August are consistent with the market fearing exactly this. What remains is the size of any reset; FY consensus of $3.28 sits above the guide, so a merely reiterated guide could also disappoint. Sized smaller because a crowded short already holds this view.
findings.independence: Same document as the tariff-upside finding (the Q2 call), read on a different line; the two are not one fact. Wells Fargo's $42 to $30 target cut on 2026-10-12 (MarketBeat) points the same way, with reasoning unknown.

findings.finding: The USTR Section 301 'structural excess capacity' investigations into 16 economies, including Vietnam and Cambodia (Carter's main sourcing countries), had findings and remedies 'still forthcoming' as of July 2026. Carter's 10-Q notes the investigation had not yet produced proposed tariffs. Management may have to flag this risk in its Q4 and 2027 commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Tariff-driven guide events cost -19.7% (2025-07-25); tariff-cost upside has not been separately rewarded.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a known overhang that the market discounts generically; the residual is whether the company quantifies a contingency in its outlook. Small, because no tariff list has been published (searched; none found by late October).
findings.independence: The Carter's 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001060822/000106082226000109/cri-20260704.htm) confirms the pending investigation; it is the same fact from the company's side.

findings.finding: The Census September 2026 release shows gasoline-station sales +28.1% y/y (+22.2% for July-September), an energy-price spike that squeezes the lower- and middle-income family budgets central to Carter's and its Walmart and Target channels. Health and personal care stores were -1.2% y/y.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Management has cited consumer 'price resistance'. There is no clean prior reaction on a macro line.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by the company; filed small as a proxy. It would matter if Q4 or holiday commentary turns cautious.
findings.independence: Same Census document as the clothing finding, read on a different line. The same release shows clothing stores +5.0% y/y, which cuts against a consumer squeeze reaching apparel so far; the size is net of that.

outside_window.finding: The Section 301 excess-capacity tariff lists, if proposed, are estimated by practitioners at Q3-Q4 2026 at the earliest, with implementation late 2026 or early 2027. Any actual rate on Vietnam or Cambodia lands after this window.

baseline_tension: There is no skew reading (null). My lean is positive, which cuts against the 5-day run-up (-3.95%), the ~17% slide since mid-August and a short base that doubled. I read that crowding as the squeeze mechanism rather than as information the market has that I lack, but the shorts have been right on this name's guide events (-20% twice), so p_up stays at 55 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1/6 (reaction vs fact; inside the guide): tariff-upside guidance cut from +1.2 to +0.8, because consensus FY $3.28 and Q3 $0.89 already sit above the guide, and Q2's large beat bought only +2.1%.
Lesson 5 (proxies small): Census clothing +0.6 to +0.4; Target/Kohl's (August prints) +0.3 to +0.2; PLCE +0.2 to +0.1.
Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): CEO-reset -1.0 to -0.8; Section 301 excess-capacity -0.4 to -0.3.
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): short-interest squeeze +1.5 to +1.3, because the same shorts were right on the two -20% guide prints.
Lesson 8 (understatement): abs_move_pct raised from 9.5 to 10.0 for a new CEO's first full-quarter call on a name with ±20% guide reactions.
Left standing: the gasoline-spike proxy at -0.2 and p_up at 55.
